briefing_2026-10-13_chirps_kenya_weekly_: Observed CHIRPS rainfall from 8 September to 5 October was concentrated in the west around the Lake Victoria basin and the western highlands at 20 to 50 mm per week, with a secondary area of 15 to 40 mm on the coast during the first three weeks. The week of 15 to 21 September also brought a local maximum above 75 mm in the east near the Somali border around the equator. In the week of 29 September to 5 October the western maximum shifted north of the lake to the highlands near 1N, where 75 to 150 mm fell, while the coast dried out and light totals of 5 to 15 mm reached the northeast.

Observed CHIRPS rainfall was 10 to 50 mm below normal around the Lake Victoria basin in each of the four weeks from 8 September to 5 October, with the largest deficits on the lake shore from 15 September onward. The east near the Somali border was 50 to 100 mm wetter than normal in the week of 15 to 21 September and 10 to 50 mm wetter in the following week. In the week of 29 September to 5 October the western highlands north of the equator recorded a surplus of 25 to 100 mm, while the south coast was 10 to 25 mm below normal.
briefing_2026-10-13_chirps_east_africa_w: Observed CHIRPS rainfall from 8 September to 5 October was heaviest over the Ethiopian highlands, South Sudan, Uganda and the western part of the domain, at 40 to 100 mm per week with local totals above 100 mm, while eastern Kenya, most of Somalia and Tanzania stayed largely dry. The Ethiopian maximum weakened and contracted southward week by week. The week of 29 September to 5 October stood out for a concentrated maximum of 150 to 200 mm in southern Somalia and for rain of 20 to 50 mm spreading south into western Tanzania.

Observed CHIRPS anomalies were mixed from 8 to 14 September, then turned 25 to 100 mm wetter than normal in the far west of the domain and over the northern Ethiopian highlands in the week of 15 to 21 September. By 29 September to 5 October the northern and western Ethiopian highlands were 25 to 100 mm drier than normal, consistent with rains ending early there, while southern Somalia was 100 to 200 mm wetter than normal. Around Lake Victoria and in western Kenya deficits of 10 to 50 mm persisted through the period.
briefing_2026-10-13_mjo_rmm_ecmwf: The MJO has recently weakened into the unit circle after several weeks in phases 8 and 1 (Western Hemisphere and Africa) at an amplitude of 1 to 1.5. The bias-corrected ECMWF ensemble mean for 12 to 26 October starts in phase 2 just outside the circle, drifts into the circle around 16 to 20 October, and re-emerges weakly in phases 2 to 3 (Indian Ocean) by 26 October at an amplitude of about 1.3. Most members stay in the Indian Ocean half of the diagram at amplitudes of 1 to 2, so the signal is weak to marginal with modest eastward propagation.
briefing_2026-10-13_mjo_rmm_gefs: The bias-corrected GEFS ensemble mean for 12 to 26 October keeps the MJO just outside the unit circle, starting in phase 1 (Western Hemisphere and Africa) at an amplitude near 1.2 and moving slowly into phase 2 (Indian Ocean) with an amplitude of about 1.4 by 26 October. Propagation is slow and the member spread is large, with a few members reaching amplitudes of 2 to 3 in phases 2 and 3 and others collapsing into the circle. The observed track of the past weeks sat in phases 8 and 1 before weakening.
